title_he: סָר אֲדֹנֵינוּ הֶעָשִׁיר בְּעַנְוָה אַחֲרֵי כָבוֹד
review: 1:1–1:4 the Arabic is Philippians 2:7–8 (أَخْلَى نَفْسَهُ … صُورَةِ عَبْد); the Hebrew keeps הֵרִיק אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ ('He emptied His soul', as in Isa 53:12) with דְּמוּת עֶבֶד, the two nouns of the epistle, rather than the Modern Hebrew קֵרוּז.

1:2 בְּעַנְוָה אַחֲרֵי כָבוֹד — the Arabic فِي اتِّضَاعٍ بَعْدَ مَجْد is 'in humility after glory'; עַנְוָה is the biblical noun (Zeph 2:3) and the 'after' is kept, because the stanza runs glory → lowliness → glory again.

3:1–3:2 כָּלָה הַפֶּלֶא / מַעֲשֶׂה נוֹרָא וְנִפְלָא — the Arabic كَمُلَ عَمَلٌ فِيهِ الْعَجَب is 'a work was finished in which is wonder'; Hebrew keeps the same two adjectives (נוֹרָא, נִפְלָא) that Isaiah uses of God's acts (Isa 25:1).
4:3–4:4 וַיַּעַל לִימִינוֹ … מֵעַל כָּל־שֵׁם — Psalm 110:1 with Phil 2:9; the Arabic لِيَمِينِهِ ارْتَقَى / فَوْقَ كُلِّ اسْمٍ سَمَا is that pair, and the Hebrew keeps the right hand and the Name.

5:3–5:4 רֹאשׁ / לְעַמּוֹ הֶחָדָשׁ — the Arabic رَأْسَ جِنْسِهِ الْجَدِيد is 'the head of His new race'; עַם ('people') is used instead of the Modern Hebrew גֶּזַע, because the New Testament's καινὸς λαός is a people, not a lineage.
